scope: Corollary 9.3 (Finite-index extension correspondence) of the manuscript “Strongly rational unitary vertex operator algebras and conformal nets” (preprints/Strongly-rational-unitary-vertex-operator-algebras-and-conformal-nets-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 280 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 b5f09142bda3ec3d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 44. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. statement: Let V be a simple unitary strongly rational VOA. Up to isomorphism over the embedded base, U ↦→ AU gives a one-to-one correspondence between the following classes: (1) normalized CFT-type unitary VOA extensions V ↪→ U whose underlying V -module is grading- restricted and of finite length; (2) normalized irreducible local conformal-net extensions of AV of finite index. The VOA class may equivalently be described by simple CFT-type algebraic extensions with the same conformal vector and finite-length underlying V -module, equipped with their unique unitary structure extending that of V . Let P be the normalized haploid commutative C∗-Frobenius algebra of U in Repu (V ), and let Θ be its transport to Repf (AV ) under the base equivalence. The Q-system extension BΘ equals AU as a conformal net on HU . Moreover, AU is completely rational and FU CWX ◦ FVOA = FCN ◦ ˜︁ FV CWX as braided unitary tensor functors with Gui’s tensorators. Here ˜︁ FV CWX transports unitary local (dyslectic) P-modules to local Θ-modules, and FVOA and FCN are the canonical equivalences from these categories to Repu (U) and Repf (AU ), respectively. In particular, FU CWX is a braided unitary tensor equivalence onto all finite-index sectors of AU .
